As soon as we have tests and enough clients (>3) are passing them, <@577788234810130432> ? Why are we talking about 6 and 7 when there's no 5 5 is not relevant for EL I believe the 7 above is referring to `bal-devnet-7`, not a glammy 7 devnet. But you started it. lol I was referring to glam 7 successful glam 5 (CL focus) + successful glam 6 (EL focus) = glam 7 (merge of the 2) im so confused lol let’s focus on glamsterdam devnet 5 We need hackmd to do summary of what is in glam-devnet-5, what changes are pending for glam-devnet-6 and what is left for glam-devnet-7. imo it would be good to have Glamsterdam main hackmd, that would list other devnet hackmds Other topic, totally forgot to announce a bit here that we now have the fully Amsterdam-compatible **EthereumJS releases** out (of course still experimental, passing `bal-devnet-7` tests). So this is an easy way to run and test certain Amsterdam features with Node.js or in-browser, this is e.g. our Twitter thread on how to test the new DUPN/SWAPN/EXCHANGE opcodes. https://x.com/EFJavaScript/status/2062162209631854772 If you would benefit from some browser visualizations/tools/... here around some of the new EIPs here let us know, we might be able to help! 🙏 The issue is that we're still trying to get stable glamsterdam-devnet-5. We dont want to pre-commit to exactly what goes into 6, but the focus would be to merge bal-devnets and epbs focussed glamsterdam-devnets ASAP so there's much less confusion, even if there's slower progress in sub-streams in the short term while we get there. We really need to have everyone on the same page now + client branches now, benchmarks + repricings + epbs + bal + whatever else we add to the fork. Understandable, i mostly looked at EL side where we closing in on Amsterdam finish line, as all EIPs and changes on EL should be finished in next devnet. Yeah we should be close now, its mostly merging everything in and focussing on hardening the fork from here on. There are still a few EIPs on the CL side that might go in, it depends on how the timelines for those look and how important they are.

Other topic, totally forgot to announce a bit here that we now have the fully Amsterdam-compatible **EthereumJS releases** out (of course still experimental, passing `bal-devnet-7` tests).

So this is an easy way to run and test certain Amsterdam features with Node.js or in-browser, this is e.g. our Twitter thread on how to test the new DUPN/SWAPN/EXCHANGE opcodes.
https://x.com/EFJavaScript/status/2062162209631854772

If you would benefit from some browser visualizations/tools/... here around some of the new EIPs here let us know, we might be able to help! 🙏
